title: Remediation orchestration playbook (prototype) — patch SLA tracker & SIEM ingest mapping
content:
Purpose:
This is a working prototype playbook for orchestration of vuln remediation end-to-end: scanner ingestion, normalization, RBAC-aware ticket creation, evidence collection, SIEM export mapping, SLA enforcement, automated verification and rollback hooks. Goal is to converge on a minimal, instrumented flow we can ship to Dedicated customers and use for Private installs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers results from external scanners (Snyk, Trivy, Qualys) and internal dependency scanners.
- Focused on software/package CVEs and exploitable misconfigs (not physical asset inventory).
- We assume RBAC v2 will be available with fine-grained actions: acknowledge, assign, remediate, verify, close, escalate.
- SIEM target is Splunk and Elastic (we standardize field names, then map to vendor index-time fields in pipeline).

Quick summary (high level flow):
1) Scanner output -> normalization pipeline (fingerprint, canonical package id, severity mapping)
2) Enrichment -> CVE metadata (NVD, vendor advisories), exploit maturity & CVSSv3 vector parsing
3) Dedup & group by (pkg@version, cve) -> compute owner team via mapping table (repo -> team -> app-owner)
4) Auto-create ticket (JIRA) based on severity + existing open findings heuristics (avoid duplicates)
5) Attach evidence bundle (scanner snippet, diff to upgrade, suggested PRs) and set SLA deadline
6) Send SIEM event / alert for infra/security monitoring (normalized event payload)
7) Track progress; if SLA misses -> automated escalation -> page on-call via PagerDuty
8) On remediation, run verification (post-deploy scan + canary smoke) -> mark as resolved/closed with proof-of-fix artifact attached

Patch SLA matrix (proposed):
- Critical (score >= 9.0 OR active exploit): target remediation window 24 hours; escalation after 6 hours if no ack
- High (7.0-8.9): remediation window 72 hours; escalation at 24 hours
- Medium (4.0-6.9): remediation window 7 days; escalation at 72 hours
- Low (<4.0): remediation window 30 days; escalation at 14 days
Notes: SLAs are business SLOs tied to ticket lifecycle (ACK, IN_PROGRESS, FIXED). For Dedicated/Enterprise customers, we will surface their committed SLA tiers and override default windows.

Remediation tracking schema (flat fields for JIRA ticket / internal DB row):
- ticket_id (string)
- finding_id (scanner_fingerprint)
- scanner (Snyk|Trivy|Qualys|Internal)
- cve (CVE-YYYY-XXXX) OR vendor-identifier
- package (pkg name)
- package_version (x.y.z)
- severity (critical/high/medium/low)
- cvss (CVSSv3 score string)
- first_seen (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ)
- last_seen (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ)
- assigned_team (string)
- app_owner (github_org/repo or team)
- remediation_deadline (YYYY-MM-DD)
- remediation_status (open|acknowledged|in_progress|verified|closed|wontfix)
- evidence_links (list of URLs)  <-- we store as repeated field in JIRA attachments
- verification_hash (sha256 of proof artifact)
- rollback_plan_id (string)
- escalation_level (0|1|2)
- comments (free text)
Implementation note: keep tracker fields flat to simplify SIEM export and DB queries.

Scanner normalization rules (key heuristics):
- Fingerprint = lower(pkg_name) + "@" + normalized_version + "|" + vendor_id (if present)
- Normalize semver to three-part form where possible; strip meta tags (build+local)
- Map scanner severities to canonical severity using CVSSv3 where available; if scanner provides cvss use it for mapping
- Collapse duplicate findings across scanners if fingerprints match or if package+version+CVE equal

Evidence automation (what we attach automatically):
- Primary: scanner report excerpt (JSON snippet with matching lines), discovered on host/container image id, and package manifest diff if available
- Secondary: suggested remediation PR link (auto-created using dependabot-like flow or a standardized infra PR template), upgrade notes, vendor advisory URL
- Proof-of-fix: post-remediation scan result, deploy time, canary verification runbook output (pass/fail), digest of container/image verified

RBAC v2 permissions mapping (prototype roles -> actions):
- security-admin: [view_all_findings, create_rules, manage_sla, export_siem_templates, revoke_access]
- security-analyst: [view_findings, acknowledge, assign, comment, escalate]
- infra-eng: [view_assigned_findings, remediate, attach_evidence, verify]
- app-owner: [view_app_findings, comment, mark_in_progress, request_more_info]
- auditor: [view_closed_facts, export_evidence_bundle]
Enforcement notes: ticket creation service principal requires create_ticket permission; evidence automation service needs attach evidence and write_siem_event but not full admin.

SIEM ingest mapping (canonical fields we emit as part of normalized vuln event):
- event_id: finding_id
- timestamp: first_seen
- source: scanner (string)
- vendor_cve: cve
- pkg_name: package
- pkg_version: package_version
- severity: severity
- cvss: cvss
- assigned_team: assigned_team
- ticket_id: ticket_id
- action: created|updated|escalated|resolved
- evidence_url: first evidence link
- proof_hash: verification_hash
- customer_tier: hosted|dedicated|private
Mapping to Splunk (index-time):
- splunk_field_event_id = event_id
- splunk_field_severity = severity
- splunk_field_cve = vendor_cve
- tags: [vuln, patch, remediations]
Example Splunk search to find missed SLAs (illustrative):
index=vuln_events severity=critical earliest=-48h@h | where action!="resolved" AND now() > strptime(remediation_deadline, "%Y-%m-%d") | table event_id, ticket_id, assigned_team, remediation_deadline

Automation flows (detailed):
A) Auto-ticketing rule (first-cut):
- If finding severity >= high AND no open ticket for fingerprint -> create ticket assigned to app_owner mapping
- If package has a vendor patch available and candidate PR can be auto-created -> create PR and attach to ticket, mark remediation_status=auto-pr-created
- If finding is low or duplicates existing -> suppress or add as comment to existing ticket

B) Escalation flow:
- SLA miss -> escalate_level++ -> create a high-priority Slack notification in #sec-ops and page on-call if escalate_level >= 2
- If assigned_team not responding within escalation window -> reassign to fallback SRE queues and notify customer success for Dedicated customers

Verification and closure rules:
- Must have one of: post-deploy scan showing absence of cve fingerprint OR image digest changed and digest present in known-good registry OR remediation PR merged + deploy time + canary smoke pass
- verification_hash computed from canonical verification artifact (zip of evidence files) and stored on ticket
- closure requires security-analyst signoff unless auto-verified by CI pipeline

Rollback plan skeleton (to include in ticket when applicable):
- rollback_plan_id -> references runbook (in ops repo)
- steps: identify impacted services, cut traffic to canary, revert deployment (k8s rollback / image rollback), re-run smoke tests, notify stakeholders
- pre-approved rollback owners: infra-eng leads

Operational TODOs (next steps, owners):
- [ ] standardize fingerprint algorithm across scanners (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] implement minimal SIEM JSON envelope in ingestion service (owner: Jin)
- [ ] build JIRA ticket template + SLA automation (owner: Maya)
- [ ] mock RBAC v2 enforcement tests and service principal scopes (owner: Security Eng)
- [ ] run tabletop for critical SLA scenario with PD paging (owner: Ava)

Notes/risks/known gaps:
- Different scanners report package names differently (npm vs. distro packages) — we need a canonicalization library or lookup table.
- Auto-PRs will be noisy for transitive deps; we should prefer suggested PRs for app teams and auto-PR for infra-owned images only.
- Evidence storage: attachments can grow large; we will keep a TTL and store large artifacts in S3 with links in the ticket.

Appendix: sample normalized event (for reference, stored as a single-line JSON in SIEM event payload):
{
  "event_id": "trivy|libssl@1.1.1|CVE-2025-1234",
  "timestamp": "2025-07-14T18:20:00Z",
  "source": "Trivy",
  "vendor_cve": "CVE-2025-1234",
  "pkg_name": "libssl",
  "pkg_version": "1.1.1k",
  "severity": "critical",
  "cvss": "9.8",
  "assigned_team": "payments-svc",
  "ticket_id": "JIRA-SEC-421",
  "action": "created",
  "evidence_url": "https://s3.amazonaws.com/rw-evidence/JIRA-SEC-421/snippet.json",
  "proof_hash": "<sha256>",
  "customer_tier": "dedicated"
}

If anything here seems off or you want a narrower version (policy-only, SIEM-only, or RBAC-only), say which and I will extract a focused doc. This is intentionally dense — it's the draft we can walk through in the next security sync.

Last notes: keep this doc small and iterative. We will convert parts into Confluence once we lock the fingerprint and SIEM envelope.

-- Ava
